notes: The original. A megalodon's body, and one of the two archetypes a run is allowed to OPEN with — `opener` TRUE. A first boss is the game teaching you what a boss is, so it has to be the one that reads with no explanation: it chases, and you already know what a shark does.

Faster and turns harder than the shark. minLevel is 0, so it is in the bag from the second boss onward — but `opener` is blank, so it can no longer be the first one. It used to be able to, and the reason it stopped is that it is a strictly faster shark: the same fight with less margin, which is the wrong thing to learn a boss on.

The kraken. The one boss that does not come to you: it holds mid-range, circles, and fills the water with ink you cannot see through — see systems/kraken.js. `opener` is blank, and that column is what holds it out of the first slot now: it is the hardest arrival to READ, and a player meeting it first would have no idea what the ink was for. (The note here used to claim level 20; the cell said 0 and always had, so the intent was never actually enforced.) sizeMul is under the other two animals' on purpose — much of this body's length is arm, which carries no hitbox. ownNames is left FALSE: it takes the general pool plus the parts tagged for it.

The king crab. The one boss that walks: it holds the seabed and hauls itself off it at you, so the fight is fought in the layer the chum settles in — see CONFIG.enemies.bossCrab. sizeMul is the highest in the file and that is a fact about the BODY, not an escalation: a crab's radius describes its half-height (it doubles as how high it rests off the sand) while its silhouette is three times as wide, so the same on-screen size as a shark costs a much bigger multiplier. `opener` TRUE — one of the two archetypes a run may start on, and the other half of what a first boss is for: the shark teaches you that a boss chases, and this one teaches you that the seabed is a place a fight can happen. Every archetype after the first arrives with a perk, and a floor-bound boss wants the reach one of those buys it. ownNames TRUE: a crab is not a fish and should not roll the pool's swimming words.

The mosasaur. The fifth swimming archetype and the only one that is not a shark, an orca or a squid — see enemyMosasaur in assets.js for why that silhouette was worth a slot. Fights like the shark does, on purpose: it chases, and the counterplay is its turning circle, which is the widest in the file (1.15 against the kraken's 1.7). What it has instead of a bespoke system is the only authored BITE besides the megalodon's — 62 degrees of gape over 1.68s — so its one committed attack is a thing the player watches happen rather than a number applied to them. sizeMul 1.6 makes it the longest final body in the game at 27.2 units, which is the whole claim this animal makes. `opener` is blank, so it is never a run's first boss (the old note said level 10 while the cell said 5, which let it open a run for as long as that mismatch stood): it hits harder than the shark and reads the same way, so meeting it first would just be a harder shark.

The hammerhead. The one boss that hits you SOMEWHERE ELSE — it is the only creature in the game that declares `playerKnockback`, and being thrown a dozen units off your line — further than a full strike dash carries you — is most of what it does to you. Everything else about it is arranged to earn that: the highest turn rate of any boss (2.6, over the orca's 2.4), the smallest body (23.0 units against the mosasaur's 27.2), and the LOWEST contact damage of the swimmers (38 against the shark's 44), because the punishment is losing your position rather than your health. Its head-look is the tell — a hammerhead swings that skull to face you before it arrives, which is the one thing this rig does better than any other in the roster. `opener` is blank, so it is never a run's FIRST boss — being shoved is a new verb, and it costs most when the player has no movement upgrades to swim out of it with. The old note claimed level 12 and "never first or second" while the cell said 5, so neither half was ever enforced; the opener rule buys the first slot back and the second one is deliberately left open, because from boss two everything rolls.

The trawler that shoots back. Rides the surface and shells the water — see systems/bossBoat.js. `opener` is blank, so it is never a run's first boss (the old note said level 10 while the cell said 5, which let it open a run for as long as that mismatch stood): it is the one fight that is not about swimming at something.

The yacht. A SUBTYPE of the trawler rather than a seventh archetype: the same station-keeping, the same three ordnance patterns, the same systems/bossBoat.js — it is not told which hull it has. What is new is on the deck. This one arrives with GUESTS on it (CONFIG.enemies.bossYacht crewAsset/crewCount, driven by systems/crew.js), where the trawler sails alone, so the deck becomes worth shooting at: a guest knocked into the water is food, and the sharks and the orca pod will break off what they were doing to get to him. `opener` is blank for the same reason the trawler's is, and its minLevel matches too, and shares its shuffle-bag weight, so a run that draws a boat gets one or the other. ownNames TRUE: a yacht is not a fish, and it is not a trawler either — it draws its own vocabulary, not the trawler's.

The anglerfish. The one boss that WAITS — see systems/bossAngler.js. Every other archetype in this file closes the distance with you; this one holds station with its lure lit and makes you decide when the fight happens, which is a verb the roster did not have. The tell is on the animal rather than on the water: the esca and two rows of photophores brighten through the wind-up and go out through the recovery, so dark anglerfish is the punishable window and a player can learn that in one fight (CONFIG.emissiveCues). sizeMul 1.5 is the lowest of the swimming bosses and that is about the BODY, not mercy: this animal is as deep as it is long, so the same multiplier the sharks take would put a wall in the arena. minLevel 8 and `opener` blank, so it is never a run's first boss — waiting is only legible once the player has met a boss that comes at them, and against a chaser-shaped expectation the lurk reads as a bug rather than as a threat. AND IT IS THE ONE ARCHETYPE WITH `nightOnly` TRUE: an ambush predator whose whole tell is a lure and two rows of photophores is a different animal in daylight, where the brightest thing in the frame is the sun. It joins the bag at the same moment the glowing roster does (wearsNightForm, CONFIG.spawn.nightlife) rather than on a threshold of its own, so the boss and the cast change over together. A full day is 12 real minutes, so a run always gets a window; a run that ends before dark never meets it, which is the point. AND IT NEVER LEAVES THE BOTTOM. It arrives out of the seabed (deepSpawn in CONFIG.enemies.bossAnglerfish) rather than swimming in from a wing, and every station it holds is on the floor - which is what makes the arena vertical: the surface is safe, the trap is the seabed, and a run is spent deciding how far down to go. That is also why the lure is an attack now and not only a tell. An ambusher pinned to the bottom with one melee lunge is a boss you beat by floating out of reach and shooting down at it, so the esca charges and throws one of two things chosen purely by DISTANCE - a radial that holds the seal in place for about a second inside pulseRadius, and an electric beam beyond it. Three ranges, three answers, and a player learns them by standing in the wrong one. See CONFIG.boss.angler.
